# Testing & Continuous Integration {#pkg-testing}

Testing is fundamental to ensuring the correctness and stability of our research software. In the **S3Bio** lab, all packages must follow a rigorous testing and CI protocol.

## 1. Writing Unit Tests

We use the built-in `Test` standard library to write unit tests for all our functions.

### `test/runtests.jl`
Every package must have a `test/runtests.jl` file. Use `@testset` to organize your tests into logical groups:

```julia
using MyPackage
using Test

@testset "MyPackage.jl" begin
    @testset "Basic Functions" begin
        @test MyPackage.add(1, 1) == 2
        @test MyPackage.multiply(2, 3) == 6
    end
    
    @testset "Complex Analysis" begin
        # More complex tests here
    end
end
```

## 2. Running Tests Locally

To run your tests from the Julia REPL:
```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.test()
```

This will automatically create a temporary environment and run your tests in it.

## 3. GitHub Actions (CI)

Our packages are automatically tested on every push and pull request via GitHub Actions. Our templates (from `PkgTemplates.jl`) automatically configure this for you.

### CI Requirements
1.  **Passed Builds**: Every PR must pass all CI checks (Linux, macOS, Windows) for the supported Julia versions.
2.  **Code Coverage**: We use **Codecov** to track our test coverage.
    -   **Minimum Requirement**: All lab packages must maintain at least **80% code coverage**.

::: {.callout-important}
## Lab Rule
A pull request will not be merged until it passes all CI checks and meets the code coverage requirements.
:::

## 4. Troubleshooting CI
If your CI build fails, check the GitHub Actions logs to identify the error. Often, it's due to a missing dependency in `Project.toml` or a platform-specific issue.
